No state vendor shall provide goods or services for less than fair market value for the personal use of a procurement official of a state agency – if – the vendor has sold goods and services during the preceding twenty-four (24) months to the state agency – or – if the vendor knows or has reason to know he or she will be submitting a bid or making a proposal for the sale of goods or services within the succeeding twenty-four (24) months to the state agency.

No procurement official of a state agency shall accept goods or services for his or her personal use for less than the fair market value from a state vendor who has sold goods or services to the agency during the preceding twenty-four (24) months – or – who the procurement official knows or has reason to know will be submitting a bid or making a proposal for the sale of goods or services to the agency within the succeeding twenty-four (24) months.

Secondary Employment You may have a private or public sector job in addition to your state/municipal position; however, you may not accept outside employment that impairs your independence of judgment or that induces you to disclose confidential government information.

When considering potential conflicts of interest regarding secondary employment, the Commission examines a number of factors: • nexus between public duties & private employment • whether such work is completed outside normal work hours & without use of public resources • whether the official/employee would appear before own agency • whether such work would be conducted outside of areas over which official/employee has decision-making jurisdiction • whether official/employee would use his or her public position to solicit business or customers

The Appearance of Impropriety The appearance of impropriety is a phrase referring to a situation which to a layperson without knowledge of the specific circumstances might seem to raise ethics questions.

The Appearance of Impropriety When enacting the Code of Ethics, the General Assembly included as one of its legislative purposes the elimination of impropriety. The legislature did not, however, make the appearance of impropriety a violation of the law.

RHODE ISLAND STATEOf HOPE advisory opinion

WHAT IS AN ADVISORY OPINION? An advisory opinion is a legal interpretation of the Rhode Island Code of Ethics issued by the Ethics Commission which provides specific guidance about a particular and impending circumstance. Advisory opinions are based upon the representations made by, or on behalf of, the persons or entities requesting them, and are not the result of adversarial or investigative proceedings.

WHO CAN REQUEST AN ADVISORY OPINION? A person subject to the Code of Ethics may request an advisory opinion about a particular provision of the Code which may affect him or her. WHEN SHOULD I REQUEST AN ADVISORY OPINION? If you believe you may face a real or potential conflict of interest, the time to request an advisory opinion is before you take any official action.

HOW DO I REQUEST AN ADVISORY OPINION? To request an advisory opinion, you must either mail or hand-deliver to the Commission a letter containing your original signature and the following information: • Your name, official position, and a description of your duties; • Your daytime telephone number and e-mail address; • Briefly, the name, jurisdiction and powers of your agency, commission, or office; • The nature of the potential conflict; • A summary of relevant facts; and • Any time constraints.

WHAT HAPPENS AFTER I SUBMIT MY REQUEST? ► Letter confirming receipt ► Draft recommendation prepared by staff attorney ► You are strongly encouraged to attend hearing ► Affirmative vote of 5 of 9 Commissioners required ► You will receive written copy ► Also available on Ethics Commission website ► Advisory Opinion and request are public records

Who is required to file? ► All state and municipal elected officials ► Candidates for state or municipal elected office ► All state and some municipal appointed officials ► Some public employees who hold major decision- making positions
All officials required to file must continue to file Financial Disclosure Statements until they have been out of office for one full calendar year.
When must the statement be filed? The Code of Ethics requires that a Financial Disclosure Statement be filed with the Ethics Commission by the last Friday in April . . .
or . . . within (30) days of: ► appointment to a public position; ► the deadline for filing candidacy for public office; or ► the filing of a Notice of Organization with the Board of Elections.

What is the purpose of financial disclosure? ► helps ensure that those people who are acting in the public interest do not use their public positions to further their private financial interests ► provides evidence that there are no conflicts between an official’s financial interests and his or her public office

What is the Capital Improvement Plan? • 5 Year plan that shows projects that have a total project cost of greater than $1 Million • It is a rolling plan that is submitted annually as a request to the state, typically on July 1st. Who Approves the Capital Improvement Plan? There are 5 levels of approval. They are: 1. University of Rhode Island ‐ Facilities Committee (April & May) 2. University of Rhode Island ‐ Senior Leadership (May & June) 3. University of Rhode Island ‐ Board of Trustees (June) 4. Executive Branch 1. Analysis performed and Recommendations made by the Office of Management and Budget (July‐December) 2. Final Approval by Governor’s Office (Third week of January) 5. Legislative Branch 1. Analysis performed and Recommendations made by both the House and Senate Fiscal Offices (January – June) 2. Final Plan approved as part of the RI Budget Appropriations Bill (June) How is a project added to the Capital Improvement Plan? • In order to receive consideration, all projects must be submitted on the Capital Improvement Request form by a member of the Senior Leadership to the URI Office of Planning & Real Estate Development • Most projects will have an advanced planning study performed prior to inclusion in the Capital Improvement plan to determine program, siting, massing, and, total expected project cost
What does the Capital Improvement Plan cover? The University of Rhode Island’s Board of Trustees is responsible for about 25% of the State’s total real estate portfolio.

This Center will promote both education and research in the areas of exploration, testing, evaluation and deployment of undersea sensors, undersea vehicles, and maritime based systems in and around Rhode Island’s unique surrounding waters.. • 3,000 GSF (URI Program not including TBD Private Partner Space) • $ 10,000,000 ‐ GO Bond 2020 (State Funding not including TBD Private Partner Funding) • Status: Pending Funding • Start 2021 • Complete 2024 Kingston Campus Bay Campus Allen Harbor

Ballentine Expansion ‐ Phase 1 Project Statistics: • The proposed project will renovate part of the existing Ballentine Hall and build an addition onto the building. Together, the renovated and expanded space will provide the following program elements to the College of Business: Student Success Center, Business Analytics and AI Lab, Business Application Prototyping Lab, Advanced Trading Lab, Corporate Partner Stations, Executive‐In‐Residence, Student Lounge, and a renovated building lobby • 7,200 GSF Addition / 13,600 NASF Renovation • $17,800,000 ‐ Private Donations • Status: Pending Funding • Start 2021 • Complete 2024 Kingston Campus ‐ Locus Map

Utility Infrastructure ‐ Phase 2 Project Statistics: • This is the second of three phases of work on the University’s primary utility systems. This project involves the engineering and construction of upgrades and component replacements to five municipal‐level Kingston Campus utility systems. These systems include: • Steam/Condensate Distribution System • Water Distribution System • Electrical Distribution System • Sanitary Sewer System • Storm Water Management System • $ 15,450,000 ‐ Expected RIHEBC Bonds • Status: Pending Funding • Start 2022 • Complete 2025 Utilities Overview

Facilities Service Sector Upgrade Project Statistics: • This project will enhance and reorganize the facilities within the Service Sector for more efficient, effective operations. This will allow for a code compliant and more cost‐effective Maintenance & Repair operation for the entire University. This will complete the Facilities Service Sector Master Plan, which orients buildings to create an enclosed compound that limits access to authorized personnel and screens the activities from visitors and guests that travel through the area. • $ 12,800,000 ‐ Expected RIHEBC Bond • Status: Pending Funding • Start 2022 • Complete 2026 Kingston Campus ‐ Locus MapExisting Service Sector Concept Plans from Service Sector Master Plan

Storm Water Management Project Statistics: • This project will include storm water improvements to the existing drainage systems on campus. The water flow and storage capacity of the existing retention areas, drainage channels and pipes are frequently exceeded during major storm events and results in erosion and flooding to the downstream landscapes and buildings. The drainage improvements projects would provide additional storage volume and improve channel/pipe sizes and alignments to reduce the frequency of overtopping/flooding. • $ 4,500,000 ‐ RICAP • Status: Pending Funding • Start 2022 • Complete 2025 Former Flooding at West Alumni Ave Former Flooding at Fraternity Circle Rain Garden @ CBLS Structures at West Alumni Ave URI Subwatershed

Narragansett Bay Campus Renewal ‐ Phase 2 Project Statistics: • Building on the success of the first phase, this phase will construct 5 new buildings and renovate one existing building to provide the necessary space to support both education and research for the Graduate School of Oceanography and the Ocean Engineering Department. • 179,520 combined GSF • $154,800,000 • $ 147,800,000 ‐ GO Bond 2022 • $ 7,000,000 ‐ Private Donations • Status: Pending Funding • Start 2023 • Complete 2026

Fraternity Circle Improvements ‐ Phase 2 Project Statistics: • Phase 2 of this project will focus on Site Amenities and Pedestrian Networks. The project will create a new exterior environment which enhances the communal aspect of Greek life and gives Fraternity Circle a distinctive identity as part of URI. The work will include new pedestrian walkways, new site lighting and recreational amenities. • $1,400,000 • $ 900,000 Expected RIHEBC Bonds • $ 500,000 Third Party Financing (RIHEBC debt service paid by Greek Houses on Fraternity Circle) • Status: Pending Funding • Start 2023 • Complete 2024 Kingston Campus ‐ Locus Map

Utility Infrastructure ‐ Phase 3 Project Statistics: • This is the third of three phases of work on the University’s primary utility systems. This project involves the engineering and construction of upgrades and component replacements to five municipal‐level Kingston Campus utility systems. These systems include: • Steam/Condensate Distribution System • Water Distribution System • Electrical Distribution System • Sanitary Sewer System • Storm Water Management System • $ 9,191,250 ‐ Expected RIHEBC Bonds • Status: Pending Funding • Start 2024 • Complete 2027 Utilities Overview

Ryan Institute Lab ‐ Phase 2 Project Statistics: • Phase 2 will construct a 50,000 square foot building on the northern border of the Science Quadrangle opposite Avedisian Hall. The building will have four levels, each totaling 12,500 square feet. Levels 1‐3 would be home to the Ryan Institute with level 1 being administrative and faculty office suites, conference rooms, and collaborative work areas and levels 2 and 3 dedicated to laboratory space. Level 4 will hold a campus wide Vivarium with a focus to meet the animal needs of the Ryan Institute. • 50,000 GSF • $ 65,200,000 • $ 64,250,000 ‐ GO Bond 2024 • $ 950,000 ‐ Private Donation • Status: Pending Funding • Start 2025 • Complete 2028 Kingston Campus ‐ Locus Map

Historic Quad Buildings Renovation ‐ Phase 1 Project Statistics: • This project involves the first of two phases of work to provide major restoration and rehabilitation of three historically‐ significant buildings built between 1909 and 1928 around the Kingston Campus Quadrangle. The four‐ sided green space, with a double colonnade of trees at its perimeter and adjacent building configuration, was designed by the landscape architecture firm of Frederick Law Olmstead, who also designed Central Park in New York City. Phase 1 will provide restoration of Edwards Hall, East Hall, Washburn Hall, exterior improvements on Bliss and Ranger Halls, and an enabling renovation of Morrill. • 122,303 GSF • $ 83,500,000 ‐ GO Bonds 2024 • Status: Pending Funding • Start 2025 • Complete 2032 Original Olmstead Drawing of Quad ‐ March 6, 1895 Kingston Campus ‐ Locus Map Major Rehab of East, Washburn, & Edwards East Hall ‐ Built 1909 Washburn Hall ‐ Built 1921 Edwards Hall ‐ Built 1928
